sentence: This project studies how fibroblasts that do not work properly lead to skin lesions like atopic dermatitis in mice and tests possible therapies.
This project studies the structure and function of a pentameric state of a channel and whether it is related to the pore-dilated state.
This project studies how immunity is controlled so that immunotherapies can be developed that produce specific and durable antitumor immune responses.
This project offers tools such as microscopy, imaging and vision testing to study ocular disease in animal models and test treatment ideas.
This project provides laboratory tools, animal models and imaging to study tuberculosis and how hosts respond to the infection.
This project looks at large-scale omics data to investigate the complex biology of cancer.
This project looks for patterns of changes in chromosome number in healthy human cells and studies their downstream effects.
This project studies how protein ubiquitination pathways control inflammation and mitochondria function in the lung.
This project studies how Langerhans cell histiocytosis arises, including the cell of origin and the effect of the target tissue, to test therapeutic strategies.
This project uses a mouse model to study the role of soluble (pro)renin receptor in chronic kidney disease.
This project looks for cell-type-specific methylation changes linked to HIV infection and cannabis use, using a computational method, to find possible drug targets.
This project manages and analyzes genomics data to understand the molecular basis of cellular senescence and aging.
This project tests a non-invasive way to deliver biomaterials to the heart after a heart attack and uses imaging to check the effects.
This project builds a wireless, handheld imaging system that combines ultrasound and photoacoustic imaging using pulsed light emitting diodes.
This project studies the short-term effects of cannabis use on parenting behavior.
This project studies how a transcription factor drives squamous cell carcinoma and which cancer pathways it controls.
This project tests exosome-delivered gene-editing drugs in human hepatocytes to see whether they stop a chronic viral infection and cause off-target effects.
This project develops standard methods to measure related metabolites in human clinical trials and tests whether blood and urine measurements predict tissue content.
This project studies a post-translational protein modification involved in respiratory cell dysfunction in asthma.
